back: A rock containing enough of a metal or metal compound to make extraction worthwhile.

front: How does reactivity decide the extraction method?
back: Above carbon: electrolysis. Below carbon: heat with carbon. Very unreactive (Au, Ag): found native.

front: Raw materials of the blast furnace
back: Haematite (Fe₂O₃), coke (C), limestone (CaCO₃) and hot air.

front: Two jobs of coke in the blast furnace
back: Fuel (burns to give heat) and source of the reducing agent carbon monoxide.

front: How is carbon monoxide made in the blast furnace?

back: It decomposes to calcium oxide, which removes silicon dioxide impurities as slag.

front: What is slag and what happens to it?
back: Molten calcium silicate; it floats on the iron, is tapped off and is used for roads and cement.

front: Why is blast-furnace iron made into steel?
back: It contains about 4% carbon, making it brittle; blowing oxygen through it removes most of the carbon.
